method: Zero-value self-transfer, explicit gasLimit, legacy type-0, fees above chain minimum. Discriminates on the node's REJECTION of the gasLimit field. gasUsed deliberately excluded as a ceiling signal (failed-deploy failure accounting scales with the offered limit).

probeFailureAndCorrection.firstAttempt: Invalid. Used gasPrice=0, so every tx rejected with 'transaction feeCap 0 below chain minimum' - a different primary reason. The resulting bracket was meaningless.
probeFailureAndCorrection.detectedBy: an explicit low-gas CONTROL (21,000 and 1,000,000) which must be ACCEPTED for the vehicle to be valid. The control failed.
probeFailureAndCorrection.correction: Set gasPrice = 2 x baseFeePerGas. Control then passed (both low-gas probes ACCEPTED) and the bracket became trustworthy.
probeFailureAndCorrection.lesson: A ceiling probe without a negative control can silently measure the wrong thing.

ppaCore.verdict: COMFORTABLE. No structural split needed. The 10% target is met with large room.

v0_3_monolithCorrection.conclusion: The v0.3 monolith was NOT network-blocked. The earlier DEPLOY_BLOCKED_GAS verdict came from treating 16,773,925 as a ceiling when it was only a self-imposed submit value, and from walking gas downward rather than upward. The monolith would likely have deployed at ~18.7M. The split remains the better architecture, but the network-blocks-it rationale was incorrect.

caveat: Measured on the plain EVM transaction path. Core's deploy goes through the same eth_sendRawTransaction -> consensus addTransaction path with the same gas field, so the ceiling should apply, but the Core deploy is the real confirmation.
